small_guidance:
- The conv (Conv2d 8→64, 3x3, 128x128) almost certainly dominates the 3.29 ms now that GN+scale+maxpool+clamp is fused. Tuning the existing fused kernel further (block sizes, warps) will not close the gap to baseline ~2.63 ms.
- If staying in tuning mode: try `num_warps=4`, `num_stages=2`, and increase `BLOCK_SIZE` to 2048 for the reduction pass — `GROUP_SIZE = 4*128*128 = 65536` so larger blocks reduce loop iterations. Also try persistently caching `(a_coef, b_coef)` across all `oh` rows for all CPG_C channels in registers (small CPG=4).
- Consider processing multiple `oh` rows per iteration to amortize the per-row tl.max reshape and increase ILP.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton conv kernel: im2col-style implicit GEMM with one program per `(N, OC_tile, output_spatial_tile)`. Shapes (IC=8, K=3, so GEMM-K=72) are tiny; use `BLOCK_M=64` (OC), `BLOCK_N=128` (spatial), `BLOCK_K=72` (full, no K loop), and fuse the GN+scale+maxpool+clamp epilogue directly into the conv output — write the final pooled+clamped tensor instead of the intermediate Hxw map.
- Alternative: keep conv separate but switch layout to channels_last (NHWC) end-to-end so both the conv (via at::conv2d with cudnn channels_last) and the fused epilogue have coalesced channel access; rewrite the fused kernel to one program per `(N, oh, ow_tile)` reducing across pooled window with channel as the contiguous axis.
- Fully fuse conv+GN by computing the conv output tile, doing the GN reduction over channels-per-group within the kernel (requires a two-pass design: first kernel computes conv + per-group sum/sumsq partials over spatial tiles, second applies normalization + maxpool + clamp). This eliminates the intermediate NCHW write/read of the 128x64x128x128 conv output (~128 MB).
